WHAT IT IS. One figure, two halves, lettered A (bias) and B (distortion). Columns nest three
deep: moment, then member, then parameter (k_off | N_ch). Rows are the channel count, each row
given a height proportional to the range of instrumental noise the sweep reaches at that count,
so a decade of noise is the same physical distance in every row. BOTH least-squares members hold
one column per half: they fit with the unitary current Fixed, so a channel-number comparison
against either is not like for like (EXCLUDE_ROWS, which covers `nonlinearsqr_g` as of
2026-08-06). The letter sits inside the moment's own label bar, at its left end, so it costs
no height; the three header bars (moment, member, parameter) stand `BOX_GAP` apart, which is two
thirds of the gap between members, so the nesting is read down as well as across.

CAPTION IS STALE. `Figure_4_caption.md` still describes the superseded R-vs-IR figure, down to
its own (A) (B) (C), which now collide with the letters here. It needs rewriting against this
figure, and the numbers in it were printed by a notebook that no longer exists.

ISOTROPIC. One decade is the same distance on both axes (0.212 in). That is a constraint, not a
by-product: the figure's height is not a free parameter, it follows from the width. With W of
panel width over n columns of 2 decades each, the scale is W/(2n) and the height is that times
the summed noise span of the rows. The frontier is `sum(decades_y)/n_cols = 2*H/W`; at 27.2
decades over 14 columns it lands on a page, and that is why the roster is what it is. Widening
the panels means dropping columns, nothing else.

Until 2026-07-30 the constraint was declared and not met, by 22 per cent: x ran at 0.148 in per
decade and y at 0.180, and neither was the 0.216 the file claimed. Three separate causes, all of
them layout accounting rather than design:

  - patchwork's `plot_spacer()` keeps the default 5.5 pt margin on EVERY side, so the six
    zero-width spacers between the members cost 11 pt apiece however small `GAPA` was set. The
    gap is now a stated number of points, `GAP_PT`. The same margin ran vertically, and a row
    takes the widest margin among its plots, so the single spacer holding the two halves apart
    was also putting 11 pt of white under every row it sat in: that, and not any setting of the
    labels, was the space under the moment bars, under the member bars, and above the x titles.
    The rows are flush now and what separates them is `BOX_GAP`.
  - an axis title is a FIXED width, and patchwork reserves the widest fixed left offset in a
    composition on EVERY row of it, so the colour bar's label, three rows below the maps, was
    holding 1.4 in away from all of them. It is now a plot with a width in column units,
    `CB_TITLE_W`, which is the device Luciano used in the Nature-submission figures.
  - the five layout heights are null units, so `PER_ROW` was never the realized y scale but
    about 0.83 of it, the rest going to the fixed rows. It is now calibrated against a measured
    render; see the note where it is set.
  - and one that made the axis WRONG rather than merely uneven, found 2026-07-31: each block
    sized its rows from its own noise range, so IR, which sweeps down to 0.05 where the others
    start at 0.1, carried 27.204 decades in the height the rest used for 26.000. The single
    drawn axis was therefore right for six blocks and out by up to a factor 2 for two of them.
    Pinned to the union now; see YLIM. It is also what makes the isotropy true for the whole
    figure instead of for IR alone, since 27.204 is the span PER_ROW was always solved against.

The first two were taking 1.9 of the 7.4 in across, the vertical half of the first another 0.4
down. Columns went from 0.296 to 0.424 in, so the maps carry 44 per cent more width than they
did, and at 7.39 by 7.27 in the two axes agree to 0.1 per cent: 0.2121 across, 0.2124 down.
Everything here was measured off the PDF, not read off the code, which is how the 0.216 survived.
Any row added below the maps changes the split and PER_ROW has to be re-solved: it has been, for
the moment bar, for the key row, and for every margin touched on the way.

ONE SHARED SCALE. The bias is read as a FACTOR on the parameter (10^Bconf), not as a log10
displacement, so both halves are log10(factor) centred on 0 and take the same breaks and the same
palette. That makes the two halves directly comparable, which two separate scales did not: the
left half being pale and the right half being red now means something. Clipped at 10^+-3, which
is 22 cells of 3276 (10 bias, 12 distortion; 20 of them NR and 2 R), where "wrong by 10^3" and
"wrong by 10^12" say the same thing. Recounted 2026-07-31; the file said 18 and fifteen NR, from
an earlier scale.

NOT SETTLED, and it is the figure's central claim. The two halves are put on one scale and told
to be comparable, but they are not the same kind of quantity: the bias is a factor on the
PARAMETER and the distortion is a ratio of VARIANCES. A 2 on the left says the answer is out by
100 per cent; a 2 on the right says the error bar is 41 per cent too narrow, since the width goes
as the square root. The unified line code makes this worse rather than better, because 1.15 now
reads as the same mark on both halves and is not the same severity. Note that the third quantity
in the figure, the standard error the white lines cut, is ALREADY a factor on the parameter. Two
of the three are commensurable and the distortion fill is the odd one out; plotting sqrt(Dconf)
would put all three in one unit. Cells past a factor 2 would go from 320 to 235 of 1638, and past
1.15 from 574 to 463. Luciano's call, and it should be made before the caption is written.

A CUT AT ONE PER CENT, added 2026-08-06. The innermost band used to run 0.971 to 1.03, so
everything within three per cent of the null was one colour. It now splits at 0.99 / 1.01. The
count that justifies it is in `figure_4_layout.R` where `SH_FAC` is declared: of the 975 cells
that band held, 843 sit at exactly 1 because their bootstrap interval brackets it, and the split
divides the remaining 132 almost evenly, 96 of them R and IR. It costs a little saturation
everywhere else, since `bandcols` resamples the same ramp over nineteen bands instead of
seventeen, and it costs two more labels on the bar, which the alternating layout absorbs.
It changes EVERY figure on this layout that takes the default scale, by construction; those
renders are stale until they are knitted again.

The bands are declared as FACTORS (`SH_FAC`) and the two validity criteria are members: 1.15 and
2, mirrored. So the iso-lines run ALONG a colour boundary rather than cutting a band, the bar
carries 1.15 and 2 as printed labels, and the lines need no legend of their own. Before
2026-07-30 the edges were a round log10 ladder that missed both criteria, and a line crossing the
middle of a band looked like an error. Anything that changes `SH_FAC` has to keep the two
criteria in it or that goes back.

THE LINES CARRY TWO CODES, one per dimension, and neither borrows from the other.

  COLOUR says WHICH QUANTITY. Dark cuts the fill, the factor by which the report is wrong. White,
  cored on a dark casing, cuts the distortion-corrected standard error: can the parameter be
  measured at all, as opposed to whether the error bar is honest, which is what the colour of the
  field says. White rather than a second hue because the fill is a red-blue diverging scale, so
  hue would fail for red-green colour blindness at the red end where the lines matter most;
  luminance works for every kind of colour vision and in greyscale.

  DASH says WHICH CRITERION. Solid is a factor 1.15, dashed is a factor 2, in both families and
  on both moments. So "the report is wrong by more than 1.15" and "the error bar is wider than
  1.15" are the same mark on two quantities, and the four lines are two criteria times two
  quantities rather than four separate things to memorise.

Until 2026-07-30 the white pair ran 2 solid and 1.1 dashed, which inverted the dash code against
the dark pair and set a threshold, 1.1, matching nothing else in the figure. Both pairs now come
from `CRIT_SOL` and `CRIT_DSH`, which are the criteria `figure_4_common.R` declares. CONSEQUENCE,
accepted: the factor-2 standard error is the frontier Figure 6 draws, and here it is now the
dashed line rather than the solid one. The two figures still agree on the value.

The dark pair are hairlines and always sit on a colour boundary, by construction (see SH_FAC), so
they need no key: the bar names them where they sit. The dashed of each pair is drawn heavier
than its solid, because a broken line of equal width reads as fainter than it is.

Two silent losses, both found 2026-07-30 and both fixed. The bar's tick marks had never appeared:
`cbar()` placed them with `match(v, lin)`, which demands an exact band edge and drops anything
else without a word, and `figure_4_common.R` warns about exactly that. The iso-lines had never
been drawn either: `figure_4_bias.Rmd` and `figure_4_distortion.Rmd` passed them to mapblock() as
`iso_sol` / `iso_dsh`, and merging those two files into this one rewrote the block from scratch
without them. The ticks are interpolated now, so a mark lands wherever its value falls, whether or
not the scale was built around it.

AXES ARE DIMENSIONLESS. Interval as Delta/tau, noise as the instrumental noise over one channel
time constant in units of i^2. Tick values are linear and typeset (10^4, never 1e+04).

OPEN ITEM (2026-07-30): the noise axis divides the swept label by 10, per
`../../NOISE_AXIS_UNITS.md`, which states that the label is ten times the dimensionless noise.
Luciano flagged a possible factor-10 error in this display and it is NOT resolved. If the
document has the factor inverted, fix the document first: it is the source the rest of the figure
set will follow when the dimensionless axis is propagated.

STILL OPEN: the field is drawn with `geom_contour_filled`, which interpolates and so does not
paint the outer half-cell ring; a rectangle version was tried and rejected as harder to read.
Isolated single cells at the top of some NR panels are estimation noise, not structure.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# The roster, declared BEFORE the source so figure_4_common.R picks it up; only its LABEL for the
# averaged least-squares arm was corrected there, not its member list. Order is the cost ladder,
# and the two interval-aware members sit where they belong: ILSE beside LSE and INR beside NR, in
# each case the interval term added to the level below. The two extra dirs are appended last, so
# each only ever supplies files the three frozen ones do not have: ../data/1f7138b brings
# macro_INR and ../data/a202e03 brings nonlinearsqr_g, and neither shadows anything.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR",
                    "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR",
                    macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b",
                    "../data/a202e03")
source("figure_4_common.R")
```

```{r layout, include=FALSE}
# Every line of the composition -- the helpers, the shared scale, the standard error the white
# lines cut, the block, the assembly -- moved to figure_4_layout.R on 2026-07-31, when the second
# and third notebook on this layout appeared. What is left here is what makes THIS figure this
# figure: the roster above, the two sides below, and the one knob that is not shared.
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# The two halves. `data` is what the block draws and `zf` reads the fill out of it, so a half is
# fully specified here and the block has nothing left to decide. The bias comes from battery_sim_G
# anchored at theta_sim (at the optimum it is zero by construction, because the score vanishes);
# the distortion from battery_pool_G at theta_pool. Both are read as a log10 FACTOR on the same
# scale, which is what lets the two halves be compared rather than merely juxtaposed.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "distortion-induced bias", letter = "A",
       data = bias,                                  zf = function(x) x$Bconf),
  list(lab = "information distortion",  letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "total"),  zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 5.42}
# 0.1595 nominal, MEASURED: x 0.1375, y 0.1372, 99.8 per cent isotropic, off a synthetic render of
# this same layout at 20 columns (tmp/calib_fig4.R case "20body", tmp/measure_fig4.py). Two rounds
# of three candidates: 0.152 / 0.157 / 0.162 gave 94.5 / 98.0 / 101.5, then 0.1595 / 0.160 / 0.1605
# gave 99.8 / 100.1 / 100.5.
# The same harness was run at 18 columns as a CONTROL and returned 0.179 -> x 0.1567, y 0.1562,
# 99.7 per cent, which is exactly what this file carried for the five-member roster. The harness is
# therefore measuring this figure and not a cousin of it; the 18-column case is kept in
# tmp/calib_fig4.R for the next time the roster moves.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.1595, out = "Figure_4.pdf")
```

```{r interval-pairs-along-delta}
# WHAT THE INTERVAL AVERAGE BUYS, ALONG THE INTERVAL AXIS, one flag apart in each family:
# LSE against ILSE, NR against INR, R against IR. 04_results.tex answers this at ONE cell, from
# Figure 2's ellipse areas, and reports that averaging is worth a great deal to a likelihood that
# models the gating variance and next to nothing to one that does not. That is a statement about
# the SECOND moment at Delta = 0.1. This chunk asks it of both moments over the whole interval axis.
#
# READ FROM `m`, NOT FROM `Bconf`/`Dconf`, for the same reason as everywhere: those are the CI edge
# toward the null (figure_4_data.R:199 and :218) and collapse to the null wherever the interval
# covers it, which is what the MAPS want and never what a table of values wants.
PAIRS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~pair,        ~naive,           ~aware,
  "LSE/ILSE",   "nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr",
  "NR/INR",     "macro_NR",       "macro_INR",
  "R/IR",       "macro_R",        "macro_IR")
PAIR_MEMBERS <- c(PAIRS$naive, PAIRS$aware)
# ONE NOISE LEVEL, label 0.1 (S_tilde = 0.01), which is the slice every other table in this project
# is quoted at and the lowest every member reaches. Medians over the WHOLE plane were tried first
# and are the wrong statistic here: nine of the twelve noise levels are high enough that every
# member is calibrated, so the median washes the low-noise corner out and R came out at 1.01 on a
# quantity that reads 1.4 in the cells this paper is about.
NZ <- 0.1

cat("\n=== A. bias at theta_sim, median |bias| in log10, over the four channel counts at noise label 0.1,",
    "\n       by member and acquisition interval (k_off; the least-squares arms carry no other) ===\n")
bias %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% PAIR_MEMBERS, param == "off", is.finite(m), as.numeric(noise) == NZ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(algo, interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(med_abs_bias = median(abs(m)), cells = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[algo]), levels = unname(ALGO_LAB))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = interval_in_tau, values_from = med_abs_bias,
                     id_cols = algo, names_prefix = "D_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== B. the same on the channel number, which the least-squares arms do not carry ===\n")
bias %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% PAIR_MEMBERS, param == "Num_ch_mean", is.finite(m), as.numeric(noise) == NZ) %>%
  dplyr::anti_join(EXCLUDE_ROWS, by = c("algo", "param")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(algo, interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(med_abs_bias = median(abs(m)), cells = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[algo]), levels = unname(ALGO_LAB))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = interval_in_tau, values_from = med_abs_bias,
                     id_cols = algo, names_prefix = "D_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== C. what the interval average BUYS, as |bias(naive)| / |bias(aware)| on k_off.",
    "\n       Above 1 the averaged arm is the more centred one ===\n")
bias %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% PAIR_MEMBERS, param == "off", is.finite(m), as.numeric(noise) == NZ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(algo, interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(b = median(abs(m)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = b) %>%
  dplyr::select(algo, interval_in_tau, value) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(PAIRS, by = character()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo == naive) %>% dplyr::rename(b_naive = value) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(bias %>% dplyr::filter(algo %in% PAIRS$aware, param == "off",
                                           is.finite(m), as.numeric(noise) == NZ) %>%
                      dplyr::group_by(aware = algo, interval_in_tau) %>%
                      dplyr::summarise(b_aware = median(abs(m)), .groups = "drop"),
                    by = c("aware", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gain = b_naive / b_aware) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = interval_in_tau, values_from = gain, id_cols = pair,
                     names_prefix = "D_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== D. information distortion at theta_pool, median over the four channel counts at noise label 0.1, by member and interval",
    "\n       (k_off). This is the second moment, the one 04_results answers at a single cell ===\n")
stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% PAIR_MEMBERS, comp == "total", param == "off", is.finite(m), as.numeric(noise) == NZ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(algo, interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(m), cells = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[algo]), levels = unname(ALGO_LAB))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = interval_in_tau, values_from = med,
                     id_cols = algo, names_prefix = "D_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
